name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.Representation.finiteDimensional_algebra_of_singleton_amongNonUnital
title: Finite-dimensional algebra in the unital singleton case

content.display_title: Finite-dimensional algebra in the unital singleton case
content.one_sentence_role: Distinguishes finite dimension of the representation space from finite dimension of the algebra embedded in its operators.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ satisfy the singleton condition of R11. Then $A$ is finite dimensional over $\mathbb C$.
content.assumptions: Finite dimensionality of $A$ or $H$ is not an initial hypothesis. Neither faithfulness nor separability of $A$ is assumed.
content.conclusion: The vector space $A$ itself has a finite complex basis.
content.proof_summary: First obtain finite dimensionality of $H$. The compact-operator conclusion gives injectivity of $\pi$, so $A$ embeds linearly into the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal B(H)$.
proof_steps: Apply [The all-representations singleton condition implies the unital singleton condition](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/OrdinarySingleton.lean#L48-L63) to the given condition. For a unital nonzero irreducible $*$-representation $\rho$, use the same operator map $\rho_0(a)=\rho(a)$ through the interface that does not require a unit equation. It is still nonzero irreducible, so the hypothesis supplies the required unitary equivalence. Thus the same $\pi$ satisfies the unital singleton condition.

Apply [Finite dimension of the unital singleton representation space](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/FiniteDimension.lean#L24-L66) with this singleton $\pi$, nonzero ordered unital $A$ and separable $H$ to obtain a finite basis of $H$. Hence the space $\mathcal B(H)$ of bounded complex-linear operators is finite dimensional: if $\dim_{\mathbb C}H=n$, its dimension is $n^2$.

The theorem [Faithfulness of a unital singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/Faithful.lean#L67-L108) gives injectivity of the same complex-linear $\pi$. Thus $$A\mathrel{\mathop{\hookrightarrow}^{\pi}}\mathcal B(H),\qquad \dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal B(H)<\infty.$$ An injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space forces its domain to be finite dimensional. This is the final step of [Finite dimension of the faithfully represented algebra](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Representation/FiniteDimension.lean#L68-L81), which the exact theorem applies after Step 1.
